scenarios.description: With no optional preferences, the beginner profile remains usable.
Intermediate defaults should use suggested techniques without invented preferences.
Advanced defaults should remain within the suggested algorithm family.
A graph learner with prior attempts should receive a useful next step without treating an open as a solve.
Solved, dismissed, and recently recommended items remain separate facts when a new practice batch is built.
A longer history should keep solved problems out while using attempted topics for a measured revision path.
When attempted and solved history conflicts for one problem, the recommendation set must not reintroduce that solved item.
A solved and dismissed record must not outweigh valid unsolved alternatives in the next batch.
Recent recommendation history must not restore a problem whose solved evidence is already present.
Ranking context may use explicit learning preferences without exposing a provider handle or learner identifier.

profile.recommendationPreference: Do not infer or disclose private progress beyond the evidence I explicitly provide.

scenarios.description: A learner correction should leave the next ranking grounded in the current attempted topic rather than an obsolete solved claim.
After a corrected recent recommendation, prefer a new valid item while preserving the learner's topic and difficulty context.
Corrected high-level progress should keep recommendations explainable and avoid inventing a stronger status.
A removed learner item must not be selected again when the remaining catalog is still useful.
Solved and removed records stay out of a later batch without erasing valid alternatives.
Deleting a recent recommendation should allow a fresh, relevant replacement without changing learner difficulty.
Relevant graph metadata should outrank a popular but unrelated title and cover the requested retrieval groups.
A dynamic-programming retrieval set should reward semantically close state variants rather than exact-title popularity.
Fundamentals retrieval should balance close array techniques while excluding an expert distraction.
A ranking fallback remains usable when provider metadata omits optional rating and popularity fields.
When all optional popularity signals are absent, deterministic ordering still respects topic and difficulty metadata.
If AI ranking is unavailable or malformed, the safe candidate set remains available for deterministic fallback ranking.
Permitted public provider statistics should inform context without turning an outbound open into verified completion.
Verified provider activity is a separate signal from manual status and should not erase the learner's other evidence.
A permitted provider refresh can improve evidence-backed context while preserving safe ranking and canonical metadata boundaries.
